notes: Fixes both root causes: a reusable caller without a task now derives its status from its children, so it stays cancelling until the runner acknowledges, and cancelRun always settles the run and emits the concurrency group when no job was updated. It adds strong model and service tests (nested depths, full runner acknowledgement, already-stuck runs); minor concerns are the duplicated no-children cancel path, `SettleRunAfterCancel` now being called unconditionally after only a comment change, and callers possibly aggregating to a non-cancelled status such as failure.

A task-less reusable caller now takes its status from its children, so it stays cancelling until the last child is acknowledged; the run is now always re-settled after a cancel, and the waiting concurrency group is woken when no job update did so. This fixes both symptoms at the root and is well tested: nested depth 1 and 2 with the full runner handshake, plus force-cancel and settled-run emission. Minor drawbacks are that the direct-cancel code is duplicated in the no-children branch and that the ordering assumptions are only partly made explicit.

At provision time the patch walks the checked CEL AST and records every `ph()` placeholder name, using an empty string when the name is not a literal. This correctly handles both the `{}` shorthand and direct `ph(req, ...)` calls, escaped literals, near-miss names like `status_codes`, and dynamic names, and it limits response-based retries to the status, header and latency placeholders. Tests cover the request-only cases and the `ph` form. Minor nits: `Placeholders()` clones a slice on every round trip where a boolean computed at provision would do, and there are no tests for the header, latency or dynamic-name cases.

The patch collects `ph()` names from the type-checked CEL AST at provision time, so it covers the `{placeholder}` shorthand, explicit `ph(req, ...)` calls, escaped string literals, near-miss names like `status_codes`, and dynamic names (treated conservatively as possible response conditions). It then matches those names against an explicit list of response placeholders, a robust and well-placed fix; the tests cover the request-only cases and the `ph()` form but do not exercise the dynamic-name path.

Handles both backends the same way: symlinks are skipped with a notice naming -l/--links unless the flag is set, and with it they are listed with the .rclonelink suffix. Size is the target length, and squashfs Open honours range/seek while zip reads the member as a .rclonelink file. Listing and NewObject agree, and regular .rclonelink members stay regular. Hostile-archive safety relies entirely on the local backend, and the end-to-end test covers it only where the escape target does not already exist. There are no range/seek tests for link reads.

Implements the `--links` convention cleanly for both zip and squashfs: symlinks are skipped with a notice naming the flag, listed with the `.rclonelink` suffix, sized to the target length, and read back with range/seek honoured, and `List` and `NewObject` agree, with good tests. Hostile-archive safety is only partial: it relies on the local backend refusing to write through a dangling symlink rather than dropping archive members nested under a symlink entry, and the escape test only covers a target that doesn't exist.

The fix works at both layers: the parser strips any single-component prefix, keeps /dev/null, returns empty when there is no prefix, falls back to `rename to`/`copy to`, and splits the `diff --git` line where both halves agree; lazygit also forces `--src-prefix=a/ --dst-prefix=b/`, which overrides noprefix, mnemonicPrefix and custom prefixes and now also covers the worktree file diff that previously had no prefix forcing. Tests cover mnemonic, quoted, subdirectory, rename, copy, mode-change and no-prefix cases; the one cost is that users who set mnemonicPrefix no longer see their prefixes in the rendered diff.

The parser now strips any single-component prefix, keeps /dev/null, and returns empty when there is no prefix. It falls back to the 'rename to'/'copy to' lines and then to a 'diff --git' split chosen where both halves name the same path. Replacing diff.noprefix=false with explicit --src-prefix/--dst-prefix overrides all relevant git configs, and the tests cover mnemonic, quoted, subdirectory and space cases. One reservation: forcing a/ b/ on the displayed worktree diff also overrides mnemonicPrefix users' display preference, which goes further than the parser fix strictly needs (though the spec arguably allows it).

Fixes the root cause: it closes the leaked dup'd `os.File` in the reuse path and stops calling `File()` in `Close`, which had leaked an fd and produced a wrong name, so unlink was a no-op. It also covers each review requirement: a CAS `closed` flag returns `net.ErrClosed` on double close, decrement, close and unlink run atomically under `unixSocketsMu` so a racing relisten stays correct, and abstract `@` names are skipped on both unlink paths. Tests are broad and target the requirements, though the abstract-socket test creates a sentinel file in the package directory instead of a temp dir.

Fixes the root cause: it closes the dup'd fd in reuseUnixSocket and stops calling File() in Close, which leaked a dup until GC and returned an unusable 'unix:path->' name for unlink. It unlinks via Addr().String() under unixSocketsMu so a racing re-listen stays safe, guards double Close with a CAS that returns net.ErrClosed, and skips unlinking Linux abstract sockets both before listen and on close; the tests cover each requirement thoroughly.

Adds `Close` to the `Connection` interface, closes the agent's connection on top-level or table gather errors, and makes `Get`/`Walk` reconnect a closed connection; reconnecting clears the USM engine ID, boots, time and `ContextEngineID`, so gosnmp must rediscover and re-localize keys, and the tests for this are good. However, it edits the unrelated `TestSnmpInitGosmi` (path handling and logger) to work around a local environment issue, and the package suite fails for a reason that is not clearly attributable.

The core fix follows the maintainer design: `Close` is added to the interface, the plugin closes the agent's connection when the top-level fields or any table fail, and `Get`/`Walk` reconnect first. `Reconnect` on a closed v3 connection clears the engine ID, boots, time and `ContextEngineID`, which forces fresh discovery and key re-localization, while an open connection keeps its discovered state. The good wrapper and plugin tests are offset by an unrelated rewrite of `TestSnmpInitGosmi` (relative path, added logger), and the package suite fails, so these edits are a likely culprit.

Tracks the latest exemplar timestamp on memSeries (with a `hasExemplar` flag, so zero and negative timestamps count) for both appenders, keeps the series identity in ordinary GC and in selected/stale GC while releasing chunks, the appender and metrics correctly, and is backed by very thorough restart, snapshot and concurrency tests. Minor drawbacks: the shouldEvict wrapper has side effects (it frees chunks inside a predicate), rolled-back exemplars conservatively delay eviction, and the colliding-series test helper was changed without clear need.

The patch records a per-series last exemplar timestamp in both appenders and uses it to keep the series identity through head GC and selected/stale compaction while freeing persisted chunks, the appender and mmap-ready state with correct metrics; hidden tests and the new restart, snapshot, concurrent-append and re-compaction tests pass. Weaknesses: the WAL/snapshot replay hookup is in the truncated part of the diff and could not be inspected, chunk release runs as a side effect inside the eviction predicate, rolled-back exemplars can conservatively delay eviction, and an existing test helper was rewritten.
